idiom_name: Codable view type with a CodingKeys enum that omits fields
implementation_notes: Swift's synthesized Codable makes the projection declarative: declare a view struct conforming to Encodable and list only the retained properties in its CodingKeys enum - a property omitted from CodingKeys is never encoded (Apple's guidance: omit properties from CodingKeys if they should not be included in an encoded representation) - and the same mechanism in reverse ignores producer fields the type does not declare. What replaces the classic filter object is the view type plus its coding keys; for a value that only leaves the process, conforming to Encodable alone is enough (Codable would re-admit the field on the way in, and an omitted property then needs a default value or must be optional). A JSONSerialization or custom Encoder path is still justified when the retained key set is delivered by the server at runtime.
pitfalls: A property omitted from CodingKeys must have a default value (or be optional) or the synthesized Decodable conformance stops compiling - the projection must be designed together with how the type is constructed.
Conforming to Codable rather than Encodable silently re-admits the field on the inbound path, so an 'output-only' projection is best expressed as an Encodable-only type.
JSONEncoder's keyEncodingStrategy (.convertToSnakeCase) is global to the encoder instance: reusing one encoder across types can rename a filtered view's keys differently from the producer's schema.
Classes and property wrappers participate in synthesized encoding: a nested reference type still encodes all of its own CodingKeys, so a top-level omission does not remove a child's fields.
